title: Understand a place
summary: Find UK population estimates, boundaries and geographical lookups.
scope: This guide focuses on the United Kingdom. Both suggested resources require R and are under development. Check each dataset’s geography and reference year.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Start with population estimates to describe who lives in an area and put counts into context.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Choose the population table and reference year relevant to your question. Check whether you need a count, proportion or rate.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Find boundaries and lookups to locate an area and understand how it relates to other UK geographies.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Match geography codes and boundary editions. A lookup does not guarantee that differently dated data can be combined without further work.

guidance: Use population and geographical context together only after checking the units and dates. These packages provide ingredients for analysis; they do not provide a complete assessment of a community’s needs.

title: Explore vulnerability
summary: Explore UK neighbourhood vulnerability, deprivation and geographical context.
scope: This guide focuses on UK data. The suggested resources require R; national coverage, methods and reference periods vary. Area-level measures cannot describe every person’s circumstances.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Examine the social conditions that can make a neighbourhood more vulnerable if flooding occurs.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: The 2025 neighbourhood index covers the UK. Other flood datasets have different coverage and dates. Social vulnerability and hazard exposure answer different questions.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Add context about deprivation and community needs using the indices appropriate to each UK nation.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Check the index edition and geographical level. National deprivation scores are not directly interchangeable.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Find the boundaries and lookup tables needed to understand the geographical units in the vulnerability data.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Check that codes and boundary vintages match before joining. The package is under development.

guidance: Read the source methodology before comparing places. Use these indicators to ask better questions alongside local knowledge, rather than treating a map or rank as a complete statement of need. These resources are suggestions, not a pre-connected analytical pipeline.

title: Build an index
summary: Check your data and combine indicators into a composite index.
scope: Use your own indicator data. The browser builder works without R; humanicheck and compositr require R. Selecting indicators, weighting them and interpreting results all require judgment.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Inspect your input data for missing values, duplicates and possible outliers before deciding how to use it.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Pass an R data frame or tibble to the checking function. Review each flag in context; the report does not certify data suitability.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Build composite scores in R when you want to write and review your own analytical method.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Bring your own indicators and explicit methodological choices. The package is under development.

projectRecommendations.explanation: Use a browser interface to group spreadsheet indicators into weighted domains and export scores and a methodology record.
projectRecommendations.usageNotes: Supply Excel or CSV data with one row per area and matching area codes. Review indicator direction, missing values and weighting choices.

guidance: Choose a clearly defined question and explain why each indicator belongs. Review how choices about scales, missing data and weights affect results. The R tools and browser builder offer different ways to work; compatibility between their outputs is not guaranteed. No index chooses the right humanitarian priorities for you.
